events.what: Fisac reformulates the simple-length-spectrum form of Markov's conjecture combinatorially (integral necklaces)
Martin gives a new proof of Chen's theorem on Markoff mod-p graphs
Gore claims a resolution of the uniqueness conjecture via a Pell-type equation
events.credibility_reason: Several F5 signals together: landmark problem with no expert uptake or citation; math.GM with no institutional affiliation; cites no specialist literature (only a Quanta article); the record's reading finds the argument circular (a Mathematica-observed correspondence treated as proof).

events.what: Tao and Yang prove Markov's equation is not partition regular, a necessary condition for the uniqueness conjecture

judgement.doubts: Tao–Yang proves a consequence of the conjecture (a necessary condition); it neither settles a case nor bounds a quantity of the uniqueness question, so it cannot carry 'progress'. The Heffern '3-adic' claim was a search hallucination and is not an event. Event/credited_humans/status_sources left as written since they still describe the most relevant real work, though no event sets the status.

corrections.why: F3: the record itself says Tao & Yang 'does not settle any case of the conjecture itself' and only 'confirms a necessary condition' — a different statement (partition regularity), not a bound on uniqueness, so scope is variant; Gore's claim is set aside as not credible (math.GM, no uptake, circular argument per the record's dispute); nothing survives.
F14: 'confirmed' was carried on a non-settling row; with status open, direction is null.
